html:
A week of rioting in Constantinople in January 532 that nearly overthrew Justinian. They are named after the crowd's cry, "Nika!", meaning "conquer!", a shout used to cheer on chariot teams.

The fans of the two great racing teams at the Hippodrome, the Blues and the Greens, were usually rivals. After a botched hanging of two of their men, they united against the emperor. They set fires that burned much of the centre, including the old Hagia Sophia. They demanded the dismissal of hated ministers, among them the lawyer Tribonian, and crowned a nephew of an earlier emperor, Hypatius.

Justinian prepared to flee. By Procopius's account Theodora talked him out of it. Narses bribed the Blues to leave, and troops under Belisarius trapped the rest of the crowd in the Hippodrome. As many as 30,000 people were killed. Justinian then rebuilt the city on a grand scale, starting with a new Hagia Sophia.
